citations.quote: 5 % tumor proportion score (optional, reported per institutional protocol)

candidates.description: The percentage of viable tumor cells showing membrane staining for PD-L1, expressed as a Tumor Proportion Score (TPS).
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the 'PD-L1' result, specifically looking for the 'Tumor Proportion Score' or 'TPS' value expressed as a percentage.
candidates.measurement_definition: Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) as a percentage (%)
candidates.name: PD-L1 Expression (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: Variability in assay clones (e.g., 22C3) may influence the consistency of the TPS measurement across different reports.

citations.quote: KRAS G12C, TP53 R273H, STK11 loss, MET copy‑number gain

candidates.description: Presence or absence of the activating G12C mutation in the KRAS gene.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Scan molecular testing or NGS reports for 'KRAS' and 'G12C'. Mark as positive if the G12C mutation is explicitly listed as detected or activating.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive: KRAS G12C mutation detected; Negative: KRAS G12C mutation not detected or KRAS wild-type.
candidates.name: KRAS G12C Mutation Status
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence reports both binary presence and variant allele frequency (VAF); only binary status is proposed.

limitations: Molecular profiling was not performed for all patients, limiting the available data for KRAS status.
PD-L1 expression is only documented in a subset of the provided clinical excerpts.
The evidence consists of discrete pathology reports and clinical summaries rather than a structured dataset.
summary: The evidence supports the use of PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) and KRAS G12C mutation status as measurable baseline clinical variables in patients with lung adenocarcinoma.
